artists.name: Buko
artists.bio: Buko is a Hamburg-based painter working in layered, fluid acrylics. The works emerge in sessions of pouring, dragging and interruption — pigment moving like weather across the canvas, arrested at the moment it turns from chaos into composition. Seen from a distance they read as landscapes of light; up close they dissolve into currents, sediment and sparks.

artworks.title: Nocturne in Magenta
artworks.description: A nocturnal colour field caught between violet dusk and cold turquoise ground. Coral flares break through the surface like signals — the painting holds the exact moment a night sky touches water.

artworks.title: Undertow
artworks.description: Deep marine blues pull against fields of hot red and orange in a slow, submerged rotation. Traces of white lacquer sit on the surface like foam — evidence of a current you can feel but never see.

artworks.title: Deep Field
artworks.description: Named after the long-exposure photographs of the far universe, Deep Field layers cobalt, violet and ember into a slow drift of matter. Splattered whites hang in the dark like starlight arriving late.

artworks.title: Heat Bloom
artworks.description: Magenta and violet open across the canvas like heat rising off asphalt at the end of summer. A seam of yellow and teal at the edge keeps the temperature honest — bloom and burn in one gesture.

artworks.title: Ember Current
artworks.description: Islands of orange and red ember float on a near-black tide, connected by threads of white spray. The darkest painting of the series — and the one that glows longest after you look away.
